title: British Council moots axing 25% of workforce to pay off pandemic loan
summary_en: The British Council is considering further layoffs to help pay off a £197 million government bailout, an investigation from the National Audit Office (NAO) has revealed.
author: Beth Kennedy
title_cn: British Council moots axing 25% of workforce to pay off pandemic loan

title: QS rankings: US loses ground on research and talent attraction
summary_en: While America remains the frontrunner on graduate employability, its universities are losing ground to rivals in China and beyond as the research gap and international talent race tighten.
author: Polly Nash
title_cn: QS rankings: US loses ground on research and talent attraction

title: India’s university rise broadens beyond IITs, but internationalisation lags
summary_en: More than half of India's ranked universities improved their position in the QS World University Rankings 2027, with 18 institutions reaching record highs as gains spread beyond the IITs despite persistent internationalisation challenges.
author: Abhishek Nair
title_cn: India’s university rise broadens beyond IITs, but internationalisation lags

title: Acumen acquires EduCorePro to boost AI-driven enrolment transformation
summary_en: Acumen has announced the acquisition of EduCorePro, an AI-enabled admissions technology company, in a move aimed at accelerating the transformation of global student recruitment and enrolment services through AI.
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: Acumen acquires EduCorePro to boost AI-driven enrolment transformation

title: The Netherlands records first-ever international student drop
summary_en: The total number of international students in The Netherlands has dropped for the first time since records began 20 years ago, new Nuffic data has shown.
author: Polly Nash
title_cn: The Netherlands records first-ever international student drop

title: Ofqual fines Cambridge English £875k over IELTS marking errors
summary_en: UK qualifications regulator Ofqual has fined Cambridge English £875,000 following an investigation into automated marking errors that led to incorrect IELTS results being issued to more than 62,000 learners worldwide between 2023 and 2025.
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: Ofqual fines Cambridge English £875k over IELTS marking errors

title: One Nation seeks crackdown on student visa “course-hopping”
summary_en: Right-wing Australian senator Pauline Hanson has reignited debate over international students, calling for tougher visa rules that would force students to leave the country before reapplying to study.
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: One Nation seeks crackdown on student visa “course-hopping”

title: Nigerian agents report extortion over deposits kept by UK unis
summary_en: The PIE understands that agents are having to “bail out” colleagues and sub-agents in Nigeria who are being arrested or extorted over tuition fee deposits being withheld by British universities.
author: Nicholas Cuthbert
title_cn: Nigerian agents report extortion over deposits kept by UK unis

title: 98% of leaders say study abroad shaped their path to leadership
summary_en: US industry leaders have reported that international educational experiences acted as a long-term accelerator for leadership, as stakeholders call for a broadening of how we talk about study abroad opportunities.
author: Polly Nash
title_cn: 98% of leaders say study abroad shaped their path to leadership

title: Nigeria lifts tuition remittance cap even as visa concerns persist
summary_en: The Central Bank of Nigeria has increased the maximum tuition fee remittance for students studying abroad from $15,000 to $25,000 per semester, though experts say access to visas and funding remains a greater concern for many prospective students.
author: Abhishek Nair
title_cn: Nigeria lifts tuition remittance cap even as visa concerns persist
